clue.text: Fair, also advisable

parts.note: fair, as in even-handed, means just
also means as well, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a plan and concludes it is fair, and sensible too.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a course is a good idea means it would be prudent or wise to take it.

clue.text: Two-faced creature with…

parts.note: the Roman god of doorways is shown with two faces looking opposite ways, and the run-on into the next clue adds that a moon of Saturn shares his name

explanation.surface: A two-faced creature is introduced, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to 2 Down: the god is two-faced, and he is also a heavenly body, a moon of Saturn, which is what 2 Down then defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of beginnings is pictured with a pair of faces, the very image of two-facedness.

clue.text: …a heavenly body and oomph — half of it covered by T.V.

parts.note: oomph is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: covered by means the piece sits inside the television word

parts.note: a television set is a telly, here in the variant spelling tellie

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Down, a glamorous being with oomph is half-hidden by the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes T from 'it'; 'covered by' has the variant spelling of telly wrap round it, making TELLITE. Oomph is sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon is a natural body orbiting a planet, a heavenly body in its own right.

clue.text: Where chess opponents sit, in general

definitions.meaning: the two players face each other on opposite sides of the chessboard
applying to everyone or everything, without exception

explanation.definitionFit: Opponents seated on either side of the board, and a phrase meaning applying universally to all cases.

clue.text: After mean upbringing ale-wife perhaps becomes rapacious

indicators.note: After says the fish word follows the turned-up word for mean
in a down clue, bringing up the word for mean sets it upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: mean, as in base or contemptible, means low
an alewife is a kind of North American herring, so an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A woman who ran an alehouse, raised meanly, turns greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' turns LOW upwards in this down clue to WOL. An ale-wife was a woman keeping an alehouse, but the alewife is also a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means grasping and predatory, like a hungry wolf.

clue.text: Chair extended to accommodate you, we hear

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take another piece inside

parts.note: something extended is made longer

indicators.note: we hear says the word for you is replaced by the letter that is pronounced the same

parts.note: the pronoun you is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: A chair has been lengthened so that you can fit in it, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'you' into the letter U, said the same way, and 'to accommodate' puts it inside LONGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A long reclining seat for relaxing is a kind of easy chair.

clue.text: Attack a foolish person

definitions.meaning: to set upon someone is to have a ... them
a silly fool, someone acting the idiot

explanation.definitionFit: To go at someone is to assault them, and calling someone this farm animal brands them a silly fool.

clue.text: Willow's got too big? That's right

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a size too big
that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone notices a willow tree has grown far too large and agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Hear about every monarch's betrayal

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for hear surrounds the rest

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is tries it
every means each
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: An order to hear about every king's act of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the word for hear wrap round the rest, splitting after its R. ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is disloyalty or betrayal of trust.

clue.text: Humbert Humbert, for instance, lends character new interpretation

indicators.note: a new interpretation of the words reads their letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic offers a fresh reading of a literary character, Humbert Humbert.
explanation.walkthrough: Humbert Humbert is the narrator of Nabokov's novel Lolita, obsessed with a twelve-year-old girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrator of Lolita pursues a young girl, the very type of a man chasing someone far too young.

clue.text: A note to be expected

definitions.meaning: a note neither sharp nor flat, or the sign restoring it
normal, unsurprising, what one would anticipate

explanation.definitionFit: In music a note that is neither sharpened nor flattened, and an adjective for something normal and unsurprising.

clue.text: Lift some of you praised

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being praised gives a person a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up is to lift it.

clue.text: Printing prominently harshly critical coverage of prince

indicators.note: coverage of means wrapping round, so the critical word encloses the prince

parts.note: a slashing review is savagely critical

explanation.surface: A newspaper is splashing scathing coverage of a royal prince across its front page.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers splash a story by giving it big headlines on the front page.

clue.text: Rustic G.P. covers entire state

indicators.note: covers means the doctor's word goes round the state

parts.note: a general practitioner is a doctor, DOC
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a whole US state

explanation.surface: A country doctor serves a whole state.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek dialect was considered rough and countrified, so the word also describes a broad rural accent.

clue.text: Change old underwear

definitions.meaning: a loose slip or chemise once worn by women

explanation.definitionFit: To alter or move is to change, and a chemise worn in earlier times was a woman's undergarment.

clue.text: Money concealed by shifty cousins I mistrust

indicators.note: concealed by means the money sits hidden inside the rearranged letters
shifty letters move around, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
P, a penny, is a small piece of money

explanation.surface: Money hidden away by shifty relatives makes a person distrustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty' rearranges COUSINS I into SUSICION, and 'concealed by' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling of doubt or distrust.

clue.text: Good luck symbol falls from a great height

definitions.meaning: the U-shaped iron nailed above a door for luck
the Canadian Falls at Niagara, with water plunging from on high

explanation.definitionFit: A shoe for a horse is a traditional lucky charm, and the Canadian cataract at Niagara bears the same name.

clue.text: Wine makes water-loving creature almost witless

parts.note: the hippopotamus wallows in rivers

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: crass means stupid or witless

explanation.surface: A wine turns a river animal nearly stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of CRASS, leaving CRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras was a medieval spiced and sweetened wine.

clue.text: Surgeons about to perform in theatre without that loader

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the surgeons are read backwards

parts.note: vets are animal surgeons

indicators.note: in means the word for perform goes inside what is left
without means the letters of the next word are removed from theatre

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, its letters struck out of theatre
to perform is to do

explanation.surface: Surgeons are about to operate in a theatre that lacks a loader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the vets round to STEV. 'without' strikes T, H, A, T out of the theatre, leaving ERE, and 'in' puts the word for perform inside it, making EDORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a dock.

clue.text: Somebody receiving a degree finally — Cambridge blue

indicators.note: receiving means taking the other pieces inside

parts.note: somebody means one, a person
a BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone collects a degree at last and earns a Cambridge blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' wraps the person round the degree and E, the last letter of Cambridge. A blue is a sports award at Oxford or Cambridge, but here blue means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent, lewd and smutty.

clue.text: Tim goes all out for superiority

indicators.note: all out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tim tries his hardest to be top dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-importance, an inflated sense of one's superiority over others.

clue.text: A vote against accepting very soft babywear

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: a no vote is a nay
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Someone votes no to accepting extra-soft baby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts PP inside NAY. In music pp stands for pianissimo, very softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's absorbent towelling garment, what Americans call a diaper.

clue.text: I am past being perfect

definitions.note: the adjective stands for the noun naming an insect's perfect stage

parts.note: contracted to I'm
past means gone by, ago

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are no longer flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists call the final adult stage of an insect its perfect form.

clue.text: Accept grant

definitions.meaning: to concede that something is true

explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge a point is both to accept it and to grant it; the verb also means to let in.

clue.text: Neat, undiluted gore

parts.note: a short is a drink of undiluted spirits
to gore is to pierce with a horn

explanation.surface: Neat spirits, undiluted, and bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, not the undiluted sense it seems to mean beside 'undiluted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for cattle, and this breed is a type of cattle.

clue.text: Music is well-known

parts.note: music written down is set in notes, and something famous is celebrated or eminent

explanation.surface: A claim that music is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune written down has been set in notation, and a celebrated person is famous.

clue.text: Duck in bath

parts.note: it looks like a rubber toy floating in a tub, but duck is the verb, to plunge under water

explanation.surface: A rubber duck floats in a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone in a bath is to plunge or submerge them in the water.

clue.text: Succeed in their careers

indicators.note: careers means rushes wildly, so the letters charge into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Children succeed their parents in their professions.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to an estate or title is to come into it by inheritance.

clue.text: To catch trout's no walk-over, that's clear

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them

indicators.note: no means the word for walk-over is taken away

parts.note: the fish word, its possessive s adding no letter
a rout is an easy, overwhelming win, a walk-over

explanation.surface: Catching trout with a net is not easy, that much is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ROUT from TROUT, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear profit is what remains after deductions, so clear and net mean the same.

clue.text: In a trance possibly 25 seconds — a journalist

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: the answer to 25 Across
ED, an editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is spellbound for about twenty-five seconds, a reporter among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to the answer at 25 Across; 'possibly' rearranges it with S into MESMERIS, and the editor follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmerism was hypnotism, so someone mesmerised is hypnotised, spellbound.
